question: Which structure helps protect your airway from food and liquid during swallowing?
explanation: The larynx includes the epiglottis, which shuts over the windpipe when you swallow to keep food out of your lungs. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T4#GNS213_U2_T4_h1)

question: Why can even a little swelling in the upper airway make it hard to breathe?

options.A: The upper airway is naturally narrow, so swelling blocks it fast
options.B: Mucus production completely stops during inflammation
options.C: The lungs fail to expand when the pharynx swells
options.D: Cartilage rings in the larynx instantly collapse

explanation: Because passages like the pharynx are already tight spaces, even mild swelling leaves less room for air to pass through. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T4#GNS213_U2_T4_h1)

question: What happens inside a person's airway when something blocks it?
explanation: Any physical blockage makes it much harder for air to flow through, which raises airway resistance. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T4#GNS213_U2_T4_h2)

question: What is the ultimate danger if an airway blockage is not cleared?
explanation: When air cannot get in, the body is cut off from oxygen, leading quickly to brain damage and life-threatening failure. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T4#GNS213_U2_T4_h2)

question: In an unconscious patient lying flat on their back, what is the most common cause of airway blockage?
explanation: When a person loses consciousness, their throat muscles relax, allowing the tongue to slip backward and block the airway. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T4#GNS213_U2_T4_h3)

question: Which condition involves sudden, severe soft tissue swelling in the upper airway due to an allergic reaction?
explanation: Angioedema causes rapid swelling beneath the skin and mucous membranes, which can quickly close off the airway. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T4#GNS213_U2_T4_h3)

question: What is the name of the high-pitched whistling sound heard when someone breathes in with a partially blocked upper airway?
explanation: Stridor is a harsh, high-pitched sound created when air forces its way through a narrowed upper airway. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T4#GNS213_U2_T4_h4)

question: Why is a bluish skin color (cyanosis) usually a late sign that a patient is lacking oxygen?

options.A: Peripheral vessels constrict to hide the blue coloration initially
options.B: The brain masks skin color changes until total cardiac arrest occurs
options.C: Pulse oximeters detect hypoxia long before visual color changes begin
options.D: A large amount of unoxygenated hemoglobin must build up before skin changes color

explanation: The blood must carry a high percentage of oxygen-deprived cells before the blue tint actually shows on the skin. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T4#GNS213_U2_T4_h4)

question: Why should you hold off on sending an unstable, choking patient for an X-ray?

options.A: Radiation exposure worsens the underlying inflammatory response
options.B: Moving the patient to the radiology department improves oxygenation
options.C: Immediate airway stabilization is far more critical than finding the exact cause
options.D: X-ray machines cannot capture images of soft tissue swelling in the neck

explanation: Keeping the patient breathing takes priority over taking pictures; an unstable airway must be secured first. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T4#GNS213_U2_T4_h5)

question: What is the very first step when checking a patient who might have an airway blockage?

options.A: Looking, listening, and feeling at the mouth and nose
options.B: Ordering an immediate computed tomography scan
options.C: Drawing arterial blood gases for baseline pH
options.D: Inserting a rigid bronchoscope into the trachea

explanation: Quick clinical checks start with observing chest movement, listening for breath sounds, and feeling for airflow. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T4#GNS213_U2_T4_h5)

question: What is the first physical maneuver to try for a conscious adult who is choking badly on an object?
explanation: Abdominal thrusts push up on the diaphragm to force trapped air out and dislodge the object. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T4#GNS213_U2_T4_h6)

question: If a choking patient suddenly passes out, what should the nurse do next?

options.B: Lower the patient to the floor and start chest compressions
options.C: Perform blind finger sweeps to clear the oral cavity
options.D: Place the patient in a high Fowler position and apply oxygen

explanation: When an obstructed patient loses consciousness, chest compressions help create enough pressure to clear the blockage. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T4#GNS213_U2_T4_h6)

question: Which medication is often given through a nebulizer to quickly shrink swelling in the upper airway?
explanation: Epinephrine causes blood vessels in the airway lining to constrict, rapidly reducing dangerous swelling. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T4#GNS213_U2_T4_h7)

question: When would a doctor perform a surgical cricothyroidotomy instead of normal tube placement through the mouth?

options.A: When foreign body removal is successful after back blows
options.B: When arterial blood gases show mild metabolic acidosis
options.C: When severe facial trauma or swelling blocks the upper airway completely
options.D: When the patient has a mild chronic cough and normal oxygen levels

explanation: A surgical airway is an emergency backup used when swelling or trauma makes normal breathing tubes impossible to insert. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T4#GNS213_U2_T4_h7)

question: What is a key nursing duty right after an artificial airway is put in place?

options.A: Keeping the suction catheter inserted continuously
options.B: Monitoring respiratory status and securing the tube properly
options.C: Allowing the patient to consume oral fluids immediately
options.D: Removing the stabilization tape every hour for skin checks

explanation: Watching the patient closely and keeping the tube secure ensures they get enough air and prevents accidental slips. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T4#GNS213_U2_T4_h8)

question: What advice should a nurse give to someone at high risk for choking?

options.A: Chew food thoroughly and eat in an upright position
options.B: Take large bites to stimulate swallowing reflexes
options.C: Lie flat immediately after finishing every large meal
options.D: Avoid drinking water during meals to prevent dilution

explanation: Sitting upright and chewing food well makes swallowing much safer and lowers the chance of choking. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T4#GNS213_U2_T4_h8)
